# Release Notes v0.10.0

**Released:** 2026-11-26

Hypercolor 0.10.0 touches more of the codebase than any release before it. Six new driver crates bring LIFX, Twinkly, WiZ, Yeelight, sACN/Art-Net/DDP pixel controllers, and Adalight serial LEDs into the rig, and native HAL support lands for NZXT, Wooting, Thermalright LCD coolers, the Razer Chroma ARGB controller, and Corsair NXP/CUE peripherals. Studio layers can now target exactly the outputs you pick, the transactional install and update engine arrives for **Windows** and **macOS**, and the REST API settles into one collection shape on the road to 1.0.

## 🌟 Highlights

### ✨ Six new driver crates for smart lights, pixel controllers and serial LEDs
New crates `hypercolor-driver-lifx`, `-twinkly`, `-wiz`, `-yeelight`, `-pixel` and `-adalight` join the builtin bundle, each with a spec (87, 88, 91, 92, 93, 94), a hardware docs page and device database entries. The pixel driver speaks **sACN (E1.31), Art-Net and DDP** through a new leaf crate, `hypercolor-pixel-protocols`, which now also powers the WLED driver's DDP and E1.31 output. Adalight covers Adalight and AWA serial LED controllers.

### ✨ Studio layers target exactly the outputs you choose, and screens become layers
A layer can now target a subset of a zone's outputs, so an input-reactive effect can ride on your keyboard while the rest of the zone keeps its own effect. A screen's face is a layer of the zone that places it (Spec 95). Studio stacks a layer on the outputs you choose and shows what it covers, layer add, remove and reorder go on the undo stack, and each screen takes its backdrop from its own zone.

### 👷 Transactional install and update engine for Windows and macOS
On Windows, the new `hypercolor-windows-launcher` and `hypercolor-windows-install-native` crates install **release units** in a journaled transaction behind a stable launcher, and recover cleanly from a power loss mid-install. Start with Windows now runs through that stable launcher. On macOS, app bundles swap atomically with `RENAME_SWAP` on APFS, every swap is journaled, and the daemon is proven by its cdhash and launchd job.

### 🔧 Drivers handle device I/O through shared bounded primitives
`hypercolor-driver-support` gains bounded HTTP and framing primitives, deadlines, `ConfiguredDevices` for manually configured devices, shared discovery admission, and a **revocable device session table**. Every network driver (WLED, Hue, Nanoleaf, Govee, OpenRGB, LIFX, Twinkly, WiZ, Yeelight and the pixel driver) and Adalight keep their sessions in that shared table. Reply size caps cover WLED (a shared read budget for the JSON API), Hue and Nanoleaf (per endpoint), Govee cloud calls (which also gain a deadline), Twinkly, Yeelight and WiZ. A `deny.toml` ban keeps drivers on these bounded paths instead of raw `reqwest`.

### 💥 One collection shape across the REST API
GET `/displays`, `/capture/monitors`, `/simulators/displays`, `/config/schema` and `/control-surfaces` now return `ListResponse { items, total }`, the same shape as every other collection route. The REST reference is generated from the OpenAPI document, and CI keeps the two in lockstep.

### 🏷️ Stable and experimental driver tiers
Drivers and protocols now carry a stable or experimental label. `hypercolor` CLI driver commands show each tier, discovery settings badge experimental drivers as beta, and the device database records how each device was verified (Spec 89).

## 🔌 Hardware Support

- **NZXT**: Gen2 and Kraken Elite v2 lighting protocols in the experimental `nzxt` family, with topology replies required and unsolicited status reports handled in stride. Hypercolor drives these devices natively instead of handing them to OpenRGB.
- **Wooting**: per-key RGB encoders and descriptors (Spec 90), with udev access granted on the exact lighting interface. Hypercolor drives these boards natively instead of handing them to OpenRGB.
- **Razer**: drives the Chroma Addressable RGB Controller, lights Blade laptops through HID feature reports on transports that keep the keyboard attached, registers the Tomahawk ATX, Raptor 27, Core X Chroma and the memory-access Kraken headsets, and labels new accessories experimental.
- **Corsair**: NXP/CUE peripherals register on input-safe HID collections, the K95 Platinum light bar lights up, and Bragi receivers gain child-slot routing primitives.
- **Thermalright**: a native HID LCD driver streams effects and faces to Thermalright LCD coolers on `0416:5302` at 320x240, in the experimental tier (Spec 96, #609).
- **Nanoleaf**: keeps panel geometry, streams touch input, refreshes panel metadata after pairing, and keeps the auth token out of errors and logs.
- **Lian Li**: a stalled wireless cluster's budget resets once delivery holds steady, and receiver address changes are logged.
- **Dygma**: the driver is opt-in. Set `drivers.dygma.enabled = true` to turn it on.
- **Output color**: devices that apply their own gamma (Nanoleaf, ROLI Blocks) now receive sRGB bytes, so dim saturated colors stay lit.

## 🖥️ Desktop App

- On Windows, WebView2 goes to the background whenever the window is hidden or minimized, so the app sits light in the tray (#605).
- On Windows 11 26H2, the PawnIO SMBus broker runs steadily and answers every request, so SMBus lighting such as Aura RAM works on those machines (#607).
- On macOS, the app confirms it runs from a stable location such as Applications before it starts the daemon or registers autostart, so both always point at the right copy.

## 🤖 Driver Platform

- Backends build from a required `DriverContext`, which exposes the installation id and the live driver config.
- Disconnect and retirement are one contract, with one generation per device at a time. A conformance crate, `hypercolor-driver-conformance`, holds every driver to it.
- USB and SMBus devices join the session table. Opens run on tasks the table owns, and an SMBus transport waits for running transactions when it closes.
- One **output policy** governs delivery, and each submission returns one exact receipt (`hypercolor-driver-api/src/delivery.rs`).
- Discovery separates observations from permission to infer absence, configured targets get reserved admission slots, and a scan that sent nothing reports an error.
- Serial transport releases run off the async runtime with fenced reopens, keeping runtime workers free.
- Built-in drivers register from one table, and default-disabled is a descriptor fact.

## 🎨 Studio and UI

- The output properties panel is one bar that fits in three rows on a phone, and the composition panel docks beside the Stage.
- Every inspector slider can be reset, typed into and stepped, and the layer blend, layer fit and four more dropdowns gain accessible names.
- The phone summary opens the Studio editor, and the phone Effects Browse view shows live thumbnails.
- The canvas draws every output, stays centered, names the device under the pointer once, and holds panel geometry during group rotation.
- Locked capture settings explain why they are locked.
- The Now Playing face and small face type are sized for fan LCDs.

## ⚡ Rendering and Effects

- Servo moves to 0.8.0 with `servo-script` vendored unmodified, keeps long-running effects lean by freeing script privates and collecting garbage under sustained script evaluation, and renders `backdrop-filter` in effects and faces.
- A zone's screens share one backdrop upload.
- LEDs a frame leaves untouched stay lit when the LED shape changes, and LED pipeline warnings are reserved for failures you can act on.
- An effect keeps running when its layer is replaced, and each composition binds exactly its own zone's compose params.

## 🔒 Security and Access

- udev grants for Razer, ASUS Aura, QMK, Nollie, PrismRGB, Lian Li and Corsair are scoped to products and their lighting interfaces, and a test models udev matching to keep every grant tight.
- Dependencies are patched for the zlib overflow in `libz-sys` and for the `url` and `cookie` advisories RUSTSEC-2026-0592 and 0594.

## 🔧 Compatibility and API

- A 1.x stability and versioning policy is published at `docs/content/api/stability.md`.
- Backups from older schemas upgrade through a migration chain, and a backup from a newer release gets a clear message naming its schema.
- A test proves every shipped config schema loads, with fixtures from v0.2.1 through v0.7.2.
- The Python client keeps enum values a newer daemon adds.

## 💥 Breaking Changes

- **Collection routes return `ListResponse`**: GET `/api/v1/displays`, `/capture/monitors`, `/simulators/displays`, `/config/schema` and `/control-surfaces` put `{ "items": [...], "total": N }` in `data`. The OpenAPI schemas are `DisplaySummaryListResponse`, `CaptureMonitorListResponse`, `SimulatedDisplayListResponse`, `ConfigKeySchemaEntryListResponse` and `ControlSurfaceDocumentListResponse`. CLI control-surface JSON output prints `items` and `total`.
- **Python client**: it decodes the new collection shapes. `ControlSurfaceListResponse` becomes `ControlSurfaceDocumentListResponse` and `DisplaySummaryListItem` becomes `DisplaySummary`. `ApplyImpact`, `ComponentCategory`, `ControlKind` and `DriverTransportKind` are each one merged enum, replacing the `*_type_2` and higher variant modules.
- **Scene storage schema 3**: `scenes.json` moves to schema 3 to carry layer scope, and the runtime session gains a schema version. 0.9.0 reads scene schema 2.
- **Scoped udev rules**: the rules grant each product's lighting interface. A copy in `/etc/udev/rules.d/` overrides the packaged file, so reinstall it.

## Upgrade Notes

- Export a backup from 0.9.0 before upgrading if you want a path back to it.
- Read the five collection routes above from `data.items`.
- Reinstall the udev rules (for example `just udev-install`), reload udev, and replug devices so their nodes pick up the new group and mode.
- On macOS, drag Hypercolor into Applications and launch it from there.
- Dygma owners with an explicit driver entry keep it. Fresh installs start with the driver off.
- The pixel and Adalight drivers drive devices you add by hand. See `docs/content/hardware/pixel-controllers.md` and `docs/content/hardware/adalight.md`.
